properties.state: {"description":"The capture half of governance, mirroring cap:kpp-proposal one layer along. An agent notices the shape of a rule — \"we always…\", a convention the build already follows but nothing records, a choice about HOW rather than WHAT — and asks the user what breaking it should cost, in language needing no vocabulary: \"if somebody pushed straight to main, should the build have stopped them, or is that advice?\" The answer is written to `enforced` EXPLICITLY in both directions. That is the load-bearing part: `enforced` defaults to true, so leaving it unset does not mean advisory, it means gate-blocking — and a rule that reaches that status by silence then owes a detector it never agreed to, which is exactly how all four of reflow2's own enforced rules got there. Also states what an enforced answer costs (unverified_enforced_rule, 0.6, until a PASSING check exists) and refuses the shortcut its own proposers warned about: never attach a verification to close the finding, because a graph node green-washes exactly like a document.","is_entry_point":false,"is_exit_point":false,"name":"A rule the project follows is captured with its consequence stated, not inherited from a default","provenance":"authored","status":"planned","tier":"operational"}
